verdicts.fix: Engine: apply the one-letter clitic hyphen to every word whose seg gloss starts with the clitic sense, also when the remainder is an inflected form that is not a glossary headword, and add lām al-jawāb لَ (seg glosses starting 'I would' / '(I would)') as 'la-'. Resulting forms: la-zaraʿtu, la-sāfartu, la-akhadhtukum, fa-sanazūru, fa-sayasbaḥūna, fa-sayazūrūna, bi-miʾatin, wa-naḍḥaku, wa-sutra, bi-ākhirihā, li-kātibāt, li-kātiba, li-aṭluba, fa-raʾsī, fa-huwa, Wa-mithluhu, fa-man, li-tanẓīfi, wa-naḍaʿuhu, wa-sanaḍaʿu, wa-ḥimāyatu, fa-kullu, li-awlādihā, bi-sāʿatayni, wa-daʿawtukum. Only the one-letter clitic takes a hyphen: the future prefix sa- stays attached (fa-sanazūru, not fa-sa-nazūru), and no ʾ is written after the hyphen before an initial hamza (la-akhadhtukum, like li-arbaʿa). No content change; the day-80 why-card prose 'fa-sa-nazūru' is explanatory and stays as written.

summary: Checked the single finding against audit/days-71-80.txt (lines 986/988 and 2549-2762), content/days/day80.json and src/lang/ar/tap.ts. 0 AGREE, 1 CHANGE, 0 DISAGREE. The engine inconsistency is real (fused wa/fa/bi/li/la forms next to hyphenated ones in the same line, most visibly on day 80 where la- and fa- are the lesson topic). The fix is changed to one consistent form: a hyphen after the one-letter clitic only (fa-sanazūru, not fa-sa-nazūru), no ʾ after the hyphen (la-akhadhtukum), and an explicit lām al-jawāb 'la-' rule, since the current clitic table only knows li- with kasra. No Arabic content changes. The reviewer's notes (empty brackets, two pronunciation quizzes whose ⟶ line shows the answer, masculine يَعْنِي after a quoted feminine maṣdar, حَتَّى أَبُوكُمَا) are rightly notes, not errors.
